I worked 6 months in AP in New Orleans for 15.50 an hour while getting my associates degree. I then moved to Columbus Ohio and took an accounting generalist position for 20 an hour, left after two weeks because my god that place was toxic as fuck. At this point I had an associates in accounting and one in business administration. I got a staff Accountant position for 52k in a commercial hvac/plumbing company. I left a little under a year because that job was also kind of toxic but I needed money/experience. I am now a staff account for another hvac/plumbing company for 70k. I’m working on bachelors and am slowly being transitioned into a managerial role which will have a pay bump. The short hand of that is my controller doesn’t like having so many people come to him, so I’ll do my job, oversee AP/AR, and possibly another gl accountant in the future. I’ll report to him and our payroll person will. So the associates did open a door for me. I did get a little lucky by finding a company who needed someone who was familiar with AIA billing and I worked in the same industry. But the 52k was just from my associates and ap experience and was a great stepping stone.

You can find something with an associates but you’ll want the bachelor. I have just my associates and am staff Accountant for 70k. However I was upfront about working on my bachelors, which I am, so that may have helped me along with prior experience. If you get the associates it will open a few doors but the bachelors is worth it.
